known_final_diagnosis: Together, due to these data in combination with Ki-67 expression (90% positivity) (Fig. 3D), which is suggestive of active proliferation, the patient was diagnosed with DLBCL. report.source_text: Gross pathological examination revealed an area of broken gray-white tissue (2.5 × 2 × 1 cm) with partial hyperemia, no capsule, and gray-white matter on the cut surface. Under low magnification, the brain tissue was diffusely infiltrated and severely damaged by many large lymphoid cells and no lymphoid follicle structures were observed (Fig. 2A). Additionally, local tumor interstitial microvascular proliferation, tumor cell arrangement around the blood vessels (Fig. 2B), and tumor cell infiltration of the blood vessel’s intracavity were noted. Under high magnification, the tumor cells were medium to large, round or oval, possessed clear nuclear membranes, displayed different nuclear staining characteristics, were variably vacuolated or possessing of irregular mass, exhibited nucleoli, and had 1 to 3 nucleoli with central or near nuclear membranes, cytoplasmic dichromatic or basophilic cells, centroblast-like and immunoblastic-like cells, and pathological mitotic cells are shown (Fig. 2C). From these morphological data, lymphoma was diagnosed, specifically favoring DLBCL.

report.source_text: After the patient was diagnosed with lymphoma, he was transferred to the cancer hospital for chemotherapy. The patient was given high-dose methotrexate combined with temozolomide. The specific intravenous dosage of methotrexate (D1) was 4.5 g, and the specific oral dosage of temozolomide was 150 mg − 200 mg − 200 mg − 200 mg − 200 mg − 200 mg − 200 mg − 200 mg (D1-5). Urine PH was monitored during chemotherapy and was found to fall in the normal range. Additionally, the blood concentration of methotrexate was closely monitored. After 2 rounds of chemotherapy, the disease progressed rapidly and the patient died 4 months after the operation.

clinician.final_diagnosis: CD20-negative diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) of the brain
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old female presented with a headache lasting more than 10 days without systemic B symptoms. Neuroimaging revealed an irregular mass (31 × 27 × 20 mm) in the right temporal lobe with uneven enhancement, large non-enhanced edema, and mass effect causing compression of the lateral and third ventricles with midline shift. HIV and HHV-8 serology were negative. Brain biopsy was performed and histopathological examination revealed diffuse infiltration by large lymphoid cells with no lymphoid follicles, microvascular proliferation, perivascular arrangement, and morphological features consistent with DLBCL (medium to large round/oval cells with clear nuclear membranes, variable vacuolation, nucleoli, and pathological mitotic figures including centroblast-like and immunoblastic-like cells). Immunohistochemical staining showed Ki-67 expression of 90% positivity indicating active proliferation. CD20 and CD21 staining were initially negative; upon repeat testing with robust positive controls, CD20 remained negative (positive control strongly positive), and CD20-positive reactive lymphocytes were identified in surrounding brain tissue, excluding false negatives. Combined with morphological features and reliable immunohistochemical indicators, a definitive diagnosis of CD20-negative DLBCL was established. The patient was transferred to a cancer hospital and received high-dose methotrexate (4.5 g intravenously on day 1) combined with temozolomide (150-200 mg orally on days 1-5). After 2 rounds of chemotherapy, the disease progressed rapidly and the patient died 4 months after the operation.
